research_question: What is the effect of remotely delivered cognitive behavioural therapy compared with treatment as usual or waiting-list control on functional disability at the end of treatment in adults with chronic non-headache pain?
control_label: Treatment as usual or waiting-list control
outcome_description: Functional disability or physical functioning at the end of treatment (immediate post-treatment assessment)
positive_direction: A positive effect indicates greater reduction in disability (less functional disability, favouring remotely delivered CBT)
search_queries: remote internet CBT chronic pain disability trial
digital cognitive behavioral therapy chronic pain functional disability randomized
telehealth CBT chronic low back pain fibromyalgia disability controlled trial
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trials evaluating remotely delivered CBT (internet, app, telephone, or video-delivered) compared to treatment as usual, waiting list, or usual care plus waiting list
Adults (aged 18 or older) with chronic non-headache pain conditions (such as low back pain, fibromyalgia, osteoarthritis, or mixed chronic pain)
Quantitative assessment of functional disability or physical functioning measured at the immediate post-treatment endpoint
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, protocols, editorials, and theoretical papers are excluded)
No comparison between remotely delivered CBT and an inactive/usual care control (e.g. trials comparing solely against an active psychological therapy or attention control)
No quantitative outcome data on functional disability or physical function suitable for effect size calculation
Studies in pediatric populations (<18 years), exclusively headache/migraine populations, or involving face-to-face CBT delivery
moderators_to_extract: Degree of therapist guidance (guided vs. unguided/self-directed)
Control condition type (waiting list vs. treatment as usual)
Specific disability scale used (e.g. RMDQ, PDI, Oswestry, SF-36 PF)
effect_size_note: Extracted as post-treatment mean, SD, and N per arm. Disability measures where higher scores indicate worse disability are retained in raw form; physical functioning scales where higher scores indicate better functioning are reversed (multiplied by -1) prior to pooling so all scales align in direction.
